author: DTrim99
body:
Two parts here:

**The $125 food sales tax credit — PolicyEngine does allow it.** The current output (policyengine-us 1.824.8) shows the food sales tax credit (the `sctc` column) = $125, and Kansas tax after credits (`siitax`) = $212.66 = $337.66 − $125 — which matches your K-40 exactly (line 18 Food Sales Tax Credit = $125, line 19 tax balance = $212). So PE and TaxAct agree. If you saw PE give $0, it was likely a stale build; on the current version PE applies it (age 76 ≥ 55, AGI $17,492 under the limit → 1 exemption × $125).

**The property tax refund (Homestead / SAFESR) — PE doesn't model it, and leaving it out seems right for now.** You're right that this taxpayer would likely qualify — SAFESR refunds 75% of property tax (~$1,377 here) for low-income seniors — but it's claimed on a separate form (K-40PT / K-40H), not the K-40, and eligibility turns on the home's appraised value (SAFESR caps it at $350,000), which the TAXSIM input doesn't carry. PolicyEngine doesn't currently model either Kansas property-tax-refund program, so like TaxAct it returns $0. Given the missing assessed-value input, omitting it is reasonable; we could add SAFESR/Homestead later if there were a home-value field to key it on.
